# Defect classes - the .txt half (RETIRED LIST, PARKED)

**This file is from the pipeline before 16 Nov and its four classes are PARKED, not OPEN.**

Why, in full, because parking a class is not nothing:

  * It was generated by `classify.py` from `BASELINE.md`. Both are retired; nothing writes
    either of them any more. The file has been sitting at "Documents measured: 211 of 211"
    while the corpus is 213.
  * Its class names - `t01_word_accuracy`, `t02_position`, `t03_symbols`, `t04_structure` -
    are verify_txt check ids, not the problem names the current classifier uses.
  * `round.py class_files()` reads this file, so `open_classes()` counted its four OPEN rows
    on top of the 92 real ones. **`--close-round` therefore refused with "96 classes still
    OPEN" and would have refused for ever: rounds 2 and 3 could never have happened and
    `done` could never have been reached.** Found by simulating the round-2 transition, not
    by reading the code.

**THE REAL GAP THIS LEAVES, STATED PLAINLY: the .txt half has no classifier in the current
pipeline.** The classifier writes `benchmarks/DEFECT-CLASSES.md` for the .docx half only.
`.txt` output quality is therefore measured (verify_txt.py, 12 checks, advisory in gate.py)
but its defects are not classified and not handed to the fixer. Parking these four rows
unblocks the round; it does not fix that gap. A .txt classifier is outstanding work.

The rows below are kept rather than deleted so the history and the reason survive.
